question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - z &=2 \\ 7 x - 7 z &=14 \\ 2 y - 4 z &=8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 7 & 0 & -7 & 14 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 8\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-7\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 8\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. The entry above the second pivot is already zero, so this is already reduced row echelon form.

$$
M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - z &=2 \\ y - 2 z &=4 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=z + 2 \\ y &=2 z + 4 \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}z + 2 \\ 2 z + 4 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$
